notes: Initial cleavages, activity abolished immediately. P1' = Ile,Ile,Val, canonical M4.
Only this bond hydrolysed efficiently. Single-site cut, the cleanest rank-1 test in the table.

Degraded and inactivated (Schmidtchen 2002, doi 10.1046/j.1365-2958.2002.03146.x). Sites INFERRED by mapping Stromstedt 2009 Table 1 sites 1,2,3 (marked PE) from EFK17 onto LL-37, since EFK17 = LL-37(16-32). INCOMPLETE: Stromstedt states PE plus aureolysin have nine collective sites within 20 residues of the C terminus, so more exist.
E. faecalis gelatinase. Third M4 enzyme, useful for testing that one family matrix generalises across organisms.
Proteus mirabilis metalloprotease. Not ESKAPE, kept as an out-of-family negative for the M4 matrices.
V8 product, refractory to further V8 cleavage, retains anti-S. aureus activity. Protease-conditional stable control.
Sites mapped from the parent onto the fragment by homology, not measured on the fragment itself. NOT PUBLISHED AS BONDS for this peptide.

Table 1 sites 2 and 4. NOTE this differs from a naive LL-37 homology mapping, which would give R4|I5 and R8|I9; the source assigns site 3 (R8|I9) to P. aeruginosa elastase only. Assay 136 uM peptide, 300:1 peptide:enzyme, 4 h at 37 C, SDS-PAGE densitometry, readout = % undegraded (<20% for EFK17).
Table 1 site 1. Source states V8 cleaves only at sites with an anionic P1, consistent with E1.
Table 1 sites 1, 2 and 3.
Human neutrophil elastase. Source states HNE target affinity is governed by P1' with preference cationic or aliphatic > aromatic >> anionic, d-enantiomer, or proline.
Table 1 marks four sites: 1 = V8 + PE, 2 = aureolysin + PE, 3 = PE, 4 = aureolysin. The four bonds coincide with the W-substitution positions (P1' at 2,5,9,12).

Four Trp substitutions at the P1' residues, all-L, length-matched to EFK17. Significantly increased undegraded fraction. MIC also IMPROVED 4-8x (EFK17 80/80/80/40/20 uM vs EFK17-W 10/20/10/5/5 uM across Pa ATCC 27853, Pa 15159, Sa ATCC 29213, Sa FDA 486, Sa 2844; LL-37 2.5/2.5/5/2.5/5). CAVEAT the source offers two mechanisms for the stability gain: the specificity pocket cannot accommodate the indole, OR increased W-driven oligomerisation. Only the first is visible to a PSSM.
Stabilised. Same two-mechanism caveat as the aureolysin row.
Stabilised. Source attributes this to the HNE specificity pocket being unable to accommodate the indole side chain.

NOT stabilised, the one enzyme of four unaffected by the W substitutions. Source gives the mechanism: PE has high affinity for the other two aromatics F and Y at P1' and also accommodates W, whereas aureolysin and V8 do not. The sharpest protease-conditional test available, since LasB and aureolysin are both M4 yet must be scored differently at P1'-Trp.
Bovine catestatin CgA344-364. Cleaved by supernatants of ATCC49775, ATCC25923, S1, S2. 24 h at 37 C. Source numbering L348|S349, G356|F357.
Human catestatin CgA352-372. Source numbering L356|S357, G364|F365, same local bonds as bCAT.

Cateslytin. Not degraded by any of four strains. CONTAINS both bCAT bonds L5|S6 and G13|F14 with identical P4-P4' windows, so a window-only model cannot explain its resistance. Authors attribute it to 33% Arg and an aggregated antiparallel beta-sheet. Use as a bound on the model, not as a passing control.
Aureolysin digestion yields FYT21, which fixes the bond as G4|F5. P1 = Gly, P1' = Phe, canonical M4. Verify against the primary text before use.

Human tissue kallikreins in sweat and stratum corneum. PUBLISHED: LL-37 is processed by KLK5 and KLK7 into RK-31 (residues 7-37), KS-30 (residues 8-37) and KR-20 (residues 18-37), all of which retain antimicrobial activity, so this is processing rather than inactivation. NOT PUBLISHED: bonds as bonds, and the per-enzyme assignment. Read from a 2025 review, not from Yamasaki 2006 itself. Get the primary paper before using; it should also settle which kallikrein makes which cut.

Outer-membrane omptin. PUBLISHED: EHEC OmpT cleaves LL-37 at dibasic sites; fragment masses 2188, 2341 and 3644 Da against a 4493.3 Da parent; LL-37 contains two dibasic motifs; no further cleavage of the fragments at later time points, i.e. genuinely narrow specificity. 1e7 cells plus 10 ug LL-37, 37 C, 5-60 min, N-minimal medium. NOT PUBLISHED AS BONDS: the source gives masses, not residue assignments. Candidate bonds R7|K8 and K18|R19 are my arithmetic, not the authors', so do not fit on them; obtain the primary figure or re-map in-house first.
Same enzyme name, markedly slower degradation than the EHEC allele. Sites not resolved. Useful only as a rate contrast, not for site scoring.

Human beta-defensin 3. Inactivating cuts sit in the disordered N-terminal region; further trimming leaves a stable 22-45 core. PER-ENZYME ASSIGNMENT UNRESOLVED across cathepsins B, L and S in the source text read. CAVEAT hBD-3 has three disulfides, so accessibility is conformational and a linear-window score has the same confound as the bCTL row.

Degraded by cathepsins B, L and S but requires higher enzyme concentrations than hBD-3. Source places the cut in an alpha-helical region without giving residue numbers. Kept as the paired rate contrast to hBD-3, not as a site-scoring row.

Oncocin analogue, C-terminal amide, all-L, all-standard residues so fully PSSM-scorable. PUBLISHED AS BONDS: dominant cleavage sites between Arg14-Arg15 and Asn18-Arg19, with Arg14-Arg15 dominant in all six matrices. Only R14|R15 is entered here because the source states the 1-17 and 1-18 products come from consecutive C-terminal EXOPEPTIDASE cleavages, so N18|R19 belongs in the exo term. Table 2 also lists metabolites 1-15 (EDTA plasma) and 2-14 (heparin plasma), whose bonds the source does not name. Half-life ~20 min commercial serum, four- to sevenfold longer in fresh blood. SPECIES CAVEAT CD-1 mouse blood, serum and plasma, not human.

Cecropin A(1-13)-melittin(1-13) hybrid, C-terminal amide, all standard L residues. Panel = trypsin, pepsin, HNE, P. aeruginosa elastase, S. aureus V8. PUBLISHED: CAM-W has improved proteolytic stability against this panel relative to CAM; no sites and no half-lives given in the sources read. Citation BBRC 451:650-655 (2014); DOI not confirmed so the PII is recorded instead. Sequence agrees across two independent renderings (BBRC abstract and Sci Rep 10.1038/srep40587).

Four Trp substitutions relative to CAM (F5W, V11W, V21W, G25W by sequence comparison), all-L, length-matched. WHY THIS ROW MATTERS: it is the only chance to REPLICATE the EFK17-W result on a scaffold unrelated to LL-37, since W substitution improves stability against V8, HNE and Pseudomonas elastase here too. Activity also improved, 3-12x lower MIC than CAM and antifungal IC50 2.1-3.3 mg/L against 9.8-14.2 mg/L, which independently supports the no-tradeoff insight. TO DO get the BBRC full text for per-protease numbers, and check whether LasB fails to be stabilised as it does for EFK17-W.
